newsitem.title: USA: Exploration Co sets capital infusion.
newsitem.headline: Exploration Co sets capital infusion.

text.p: Exploration Co said Tuesday it has arranged through Sorbus Asset Strategies SA for foreign investors to inject $35 million cash into the company.

The money will primarily be used to purchase working interests in 260,000 net acres of oil and gas leases in the Williston Basin and to drill horizontal wells in the Red River formation, the company said.
Exploration said it owns a 20-25 percent interest in 160,000 acres in the Williston Basin.

It stated the capital would be used to purchase the remaining 75-80 percent working interest in these leases. In addition, the company will purchase a 100 percent interest in another 100,000 net acres in the vicinity of its existing leasehold.

The company said it will receive $21 million from the investors in exchange for a 40.8 percent net profits interest in wells drilled on the 260,000 acres together with a $4 million, 5 year debenture earning 6 percent interest per year and convertible at $5.00 per share.
To complete the capital infusion, Exploration said, it has agreed to sell 2.8 million common shares for $14 million.

The company said it will pay $30 million for the additional interest in the 260,000 net acres made up of $22 million cash, 1 million restricted shares and a 7.2 percent net profits interest in wells drilled on the leases.

After purchasing the leases and paying expenses, the company said, it will have about $12.25 million to develop its leasehold. After allowing for the net profits interests granted to investors, the company's acreage position will increase to an effective 50 percent working interest in the entire 260,000 acres, it said.
With the issuance of the additional stock, the company's issued and outstanding shares will increase to some 13.8 million.

The company also said it is drilling its first horizontal well in the Red River formation. Exploration is a 75 percent interest owner in Continental Resources' Barbara No. 1-15 which is being drilled in Bowman County, N.D.
It said the well should be finished drilling within 15-20 days. The company has permitted 9 additional horizontal Red River wells in North Dakota and Montana.
